name: Kubernetes
scope: A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in Kubernetes as a competency should be able to design multi-AZ/region production clusters—choosing control-plane topology, etcd layout, API-server HA, CCM/CSI/CNI integrations and CIDR plans—using kubeadm, kOps, Kubespray, Cluster-API providers, Terraform/Pulumi or OpenShift/Rancher. They automate bootstrap, golden-image hardening, PKI rotation, staged canary upgrades and deprecation migrations with GitOps pipelines (Argo CD, Flux, Tekton, Jenkins X), cluster-autoscaler, descheduler, kured and BuildKit/Kaniko image builders. They model and ship workloads via Helm, Kustomize, Kpt, Jsonnet, Carvel or Operators, implement HPA/VPA/KEDA, progressive delivery (Argo Rollouts, Flagger), and debug scheduler, probe or init/sidecar issues. They provide deterministic, secure CNI networking (Calico, Cilium, Weave, OVN), tune kube-proxy iptables/ipvs, run MetalLB, Ingress/Gateway API controllers (NGINX, Traefik, HAProxy, Envoy), service meshes (Istio, Linkerd, Kuma) and multi-cluster fabrics (Submariner, Cilium ClusterMesh). They operate CSI storage backends (Rook-Ceph, Portworx, Longhorn, EBS/EFS/Filestore), snapshots, cloning, expansion, generic ephemeral volumes and DB operators while mastering mount propagation, fsGroup, SELinux and quorum concepts. They harden clusters with RBAC aggregation, PodSecurity Standards, seccomp/AppArmor, capabilities, OPA Gatekeeper, Kyverno, KMS-backed Secrets or Vault/external-secrets, enforce supply-chain policies with cosign, SBOM, Trivy/Grype and runtime defense (Falco, Tetragon). They deploy end-to-end observability stacks—Prometheus Operator/Thanos/Mimir, Alertmanager, Grafana, kube-state-metrics, Loki/Elastic/Vector, OpenTelemetry/Jaeger/Tempo—and craft SLO dashboards, alert routing and automated remediation (KEDA, KEEDA, robusta). They benchmark and optimise large fleets via kubemark/ClusterLoader2, Goldilocks, VPA, OpenCost/kubecost, tune cpu-manager, topology-manager, sysctls, eviction thresholds, etcd compaction and NUMA/hugepages. They implement backup/DR with encrypted etcd snapshots, Velero/Stash/Kasten, chaos drills using LitmusChaos/Chaos Mesh and plan cold- or warm-standby clusters. They manage fleets across clouds/edge with Rancher, OpenShift ACM, Tanzu MC, K3s/K3d/KubeEdge, global load-balancing, OCM ClusterSet, Submariner GSLB and cross-cluster Gateway-API routing. They build internal platforms with Backstage, Crossplane, Kratix, Terraform-controller, maintain Git repo strategies, SOPS/Sealed-Secrets, runbook/ADR libraries, incident tools (PagerDuty, OpsGenie) and mentor teams on SRE, DevSecOps and compliance (PCI, HIPAA, GDPR, FedRAMP). They extend the API with CRDs, webhooks, controllers/operators via Kubebuilder, Operator-SDK, Kopf, manage conversion, finalizers, aggregated API servers, publish OLM bundles and handle OCI artifacts in Harbor/ECR/ACR with Notary v2. Finally, they track KEPs, release cadences, CVEs, contribute PRs/issues, engage SIGs, and maintain an internal knowledge base of roadmap, deprecations and governance.
long_scope:
KUBERNETES – ADVANCED PROFICIENCY (≈ 6-10 years of focused, production‐grade experience)

The scope below describes the complete surface area that must be demonstrably mastered by an “Advanced” professional.  At this level the individual is expected to design, build, secure, operate, scale and continuously improve large-scale, business-critical Kubernetes platforms while mentoring others, aligning with organisational governance, and integrating with the wider cloud-native ecosystem.  They are not yet a recognised industry thought-leader (that is the Expert tier), but they have repeatedly delivered sophisticated outcomes in multiple real-world environments.

The scope is grouped into 15 competency domains; each domain states (a) outcomes the practitioner must regularly deliver, (b) tasks they must perform end-to-end, (c) conceptual mastery expected, and (d) technologies / tools they are able to employ fluently.  “Fluently” means the professional can choose, justify, configure, automate, troubleshoot and extend the tool without step-by-step guides.

──────────────────────────────────────────
1. Cluster Architecture & Design
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Architect production-grade clusters that meet SLA/SLO, resiliency, multi-AZ / multi-region, performance, cost, regulatory and organisational constraints.  
• Produce reference architectures, capacity models and upgrade strategies consumed by platform and application teams.

Tasks  
• Select control-plane topology, etcd layout, API server HA strategy, node pool design, network topology, CIDR sizing, DNS, IPAM.  
• Balance trade-offs between hosted (GKE, EKS, AKS, OpenShift, Rancher…) and self-managed (kubeadm, kOps, Kubespray, Cluster-API) models.  
• Document threat models, RTO/RPO, SLIs/SLOs and failure domains.

Concept Mastery  
• Deep internals of control-plane components, leader election, admission chain, reconciliation loops, leases & heartbeats, graceful node shutdown.  
• Scheduler queues, predicates, scoring, pre-emption and topology-spread constraints.  
• Cluster-autoscaler vs. HPA/VPA semantics, runtime sandbox differences (runc, containerd, cri-o, gVisor, Kata).  
• Cloud provider integration contracts (CCM, CSI, CNI).

Tools & Tech  
kubeadm, Cluster-API providers, kOps, Kubespray, OpenShift IPI/UPI flows, Terraform/Pulumi, Terraform-CDK, cluster-autoscaler, descheduler.

──────────────────────────────────────────
2. Provisioning & Lifecycle Management
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Zero-downtime creation, expansion, shrinking, upgrading and decommissioning of clusters across environments (on-prem, cloud, hybrid).  

Tasks  
• Automate cluster bootstrap, PKI generation/rotation, etcd snapshots/restore, version skew management among components.  
• Implement staged canary upgrades, verify feature-gates, handle deprecated APIs.  
• Maintain golden AMI/OS images with CIS hardening and kernel tuning.

Concept Mastery  
• kubelet–API server version skew rules, feature-gate lifecycle, alpha/beta/GA graduation, migration of in-tree to CSI/CNI/CCM.  
• Idempotent infrastructure as code, immutable vs. mutable nodes.

Tools & Tech  
Cluster-API, Flux-CD controllers, GitOps pipelines, Kubectl-drain/cordon wrappers, kured, container image build pipelines (BuildKit, Kaniko, img).

──────────────────────────────────────────
3. Workload Orchestration & Application Delivery
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Consistently ship secure, observable, policy-compliant workloads via repeatable pipelines and GitOps pull-based deployments.

Tasks  
• Model applications with Helm, Kustomize, Kpt, Jsonnet, Carvel, OpenShift Templates or Operators; enforce RBAC, network policies, PodSecurity standards.  
• Implement progressive delivery (canary, blue/green, A/B) with Argo Rollouts or Flagger; wire auto-scaling HPA/VPA/KEDA triggers.  
• Diagnose scheduling or container startup failures, debug init/sidecar race conditions.

Concept Mastery  
• Deployment vs. StatefulSet vs. DaemonSet vs. Job vs. CronJob semantics; pod topology constraints, affinity/anti-affinity, disruption budgets.  
• Container lifecycle hooks, probes, restartPolicies, shareProcessNamespace, cgroup limitations, pod overhead.

Tools & Tech  
Helmfile, Argo CD, Flux, Spinnaker, Jenkins X, Tekton, Skaffold, Shipwright, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions.

──────────────────────────────────────────
4. Networking
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Provide deterministic, secure, high-performance pod-to-pod, pod-to-service and ingress/egress connectivity that survives multi-cluster and hybrid layouts.

Tasks  
• Select, deploy and operate CNI plugins (Calico, Cilium, Weave Net, Flannel, OVN-Kubernetes) with eBPF, IP-IP, VXLAN or Geneve encapsulation.  
• Configure kube-proxy modes (iptables/ipvs), native load balancer integrations, NodeLocal DNS cache, CoreDNS customisations.  
• Implement multi-cluster service discovery (Submariner, cilium-cluster-mesh) and Service Mesh (Istio, Linkerd, Kuma) for MTLS and traffic shaping.  
• Apply L4/L7 ingress controllers, Gateway API CRDs, network policies, egress gateways, global rate limiting.

Concept Mastery  
• Kubernetes Service abstractions (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, Headless, ExternalName) and VIP allocation algorithms.  
• TCP vs. UDP handling, conntrack entries, kube-proxy synchronization, hair-pin NAT, source-IP preservation.  
• BGP, ECMP, egress masquerade considerations in public/private cloud.

Tools & Tech  
Cilium CLI/Hubble, Calico Felix/Bird, MetalLB, NGINX/HAProxy/Traefik Ingress Controllers, Envoy filters, Istio Telemetry v2.

──────────────────────────────────────────
5. Storage & Stateful Workloads
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Deliver performant, durable and policy-compliant block, file and object storage to workloads; build database/stateful operator patterns.

Tasks  
• Integrate CSI drivers, dynamic provisioning, snapshots, cloning, volume expansion, PVC/PV reclaim policies.  
• Deploy Rook/Ceph, Portworx, OpenEBS, Longhorn or cloud-native storage backends; tune for IOPS/throughtput, topology-aware scheduling.  
• Execute storage migrations, online volume resize, generic ephemeral volumes, RWX/RWO strategies.

Concept Mastery  
• Container runtime mount propagation, bind-mount vs. tmpfs vs. loopback, fsGroup semantics, SELinux context relabeling.  
• Quorum, split-brain, consistency models of distributed storage, implications for StatefulSets.

Tools & Tech  
Velero-restic for snapshot, Stork, csi-snapshotter, csi-resizer, Database Operators (Postgres-Operator, MongoDB Community-Operator, MySQL Operator).

──────────────────────────────────────────
6. Security, Identity & Policy
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Protect cluster, workloads, secrets and supply chain against insider and external threats; pass formal audits and penetration tests.

Tasks  
• Harden kube-api server, etcd, admission chain, audit logging; implement certificate rotation, webhook authentication.  
• Manage RBAC at scale with groups, impersonation, aggregation; design multi-tenant namespaces, soft and hard resource quotas.  
• Enforce PodSecurity Standards, seccomp, AppArmor, capabilities, rootless, SELinux.  
• Implement OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno or K-Warden policies; integrate with organizational IdPs (OIDC, LDAP, SAML).  
• Seal, encrypt and rotate Secrets with KMS providers or external secrets operators (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager).  
• Run image supply-chain security: SBOM generation, cosign signatures, policy-controller attestation, admission scanning (Trivy, Clair, Grype).

Concept Mastery  
• TLS bootstrapping, x509 SAN requirements, service account tokens vs. projected tokens vs. OIDC federation.  
• Admission control order (mutating, validating) and fail-open/fail-close behavior.  
• Node security: kernel hardening, seccomp profiles, runtime defense (Falco, Cilium Tetragon), cgroups v1/v2 implications.

Tools & Tech  
CIS Benchmark tools (kube-bench), audit2rbac, opa-eval, kyverno CLI, vault-agent-injector, cosign, slsa-framework.

──────────────────────────────────────────
7. Observability (Monitoring, Logging, Tracing)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Deliver end-to-end telemetry revealing control plane health, workload performance, user experience and business metrics.

Tasks  
• Deploy and tune Prometheus Operator/Thanos/Mimir, alertmanager routing, recording rules, custom exporters; enforce multi-tenant metrics.  
• Centralize logs with fluent-bit/fluentd/vector -> Loki/Elasticsearch/Opensearch/Splunk; implement structured logging standards.  
• Integrate distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry Collector, Jaeger, Tempo, Zipkin) and correlate spans with metrics and logs.  
• Implement SLO dashboards (Grafana, Kibana) and automated alert testing (robusta, amtool).  
• Design self-healing via autonomous remediation (Kubernetes-event-driven-autoscaling, Argo Rollouts Analysis).

Concept Mastery  
• Prometheus TSDB retention/persistence, remote-write semantics, HA federation.  
• Log backpressure, buffering, multiline handling, journald integration.  
• OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, sampling strategies, context propagation across service mesh.

Tools & Tech  
kube-state-metrics, kube-events, kubewatch, Grafana Mimir, Loki, SigLens, Tempo, Alertmanager, Blackbox exporter.

──────────────────────────────────────────
8. Performance, Scalability & Optimisation
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Maintain predictable performance at thousands-of-node / 100k-pod scale while keeping cost, burn-rate and carbon footprint optimised.

Tasks  
• Execute scale testing with kubemark, ClusterLoader2 or Locust; identify CPU throttling, memory fragmentation, cgroup pressure, IO saturation.  
• Optimise pod density, bin-packing algorithms, resource requests, vertical/cluster-autoscaler interactions, overcommit policies.  
• Tune sysctls, kube-proxy conntrack, kubelet eviction thresholds and image garbage collection.  
• Right-size instance classes, spot vs. on-demand mixes, binpack vs. spread strategies, cost allocation tagging.

Concept Mastery  
• API server watch/list behaviour, etcd compaction/defragmentation, NSA and CRD effect on etcd size.  
• NUMA awareness, hugepages, swap-support semantics, cgroups v2 pressure stalls.  
• QoS classes, topology manager, CPU manager policies.

Tools & Tech  
Goldilocks, Vertical Pod Autoscaler, kube-downscaler, kubecost, OpenCost, Catchpoint or Bottlerocket OS metrics.

──────────────────────────────────────────
9. Reliability, Backup & Disaster Recovery
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Guarantee defined RPO/RTO for cluster state, persistent data and application configuration.

Tasks  
• Automate etcd backups, validate restore rehearsals; encrypt snapshots at rest.  
• Employ Velero/Kasten/Kanister for namespace-level or cluster-level backup/restore (PV, CRDs, RBAC, secrets).  
• Create multi-region DR plans, read-only standby API servers, cold-standby clusters; execute chaos drills with LitmusChaos or Chaos Mesh.

Concept Mastery  
• Etcd WAL/raft, quorum loss scenarios, FSB (full-snapshot backup) vs. incremental.  
• Disaster variants: cloud-provider zone outage, DNS failure, certificate expiry, compromised node.

Tools & Tech  
Velero, Stash, k8up, etcd-manager, chaos-engineering platforms, Argo Rollouts Analysis templates for automated rollback.

──────────────────────────────────────────
10. Multi-Cluster, Hybrid & Edge Deployments
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Orchestrate and govern fleets of clusters across clouds, regions and edge locations with consistent policy and workload placement.

Tasks  
• Use Rancher, OpenShift ACM, VMware Tanzu Mission Control or Cluster-API fleet management.  
• Coordinate global load-balancing, service discovery (GSLB, Submariner, Istio multi-primary, Cilium ClusterMesh).  
• Centralise identity, policy, logging and metrics collection; replicate secrets across clusters with external-secrets operators.  
• Apply ClusterSet topology, placement constraints, cluster-proxy for edge devices.

Concept Mastery  
• Federation v2 APIs, KubeFed, Gateway API cross-cluster routing, WAN latency impact, data gravity.  
• Cluster lifecycle drift detection, hub-and-spoke vs. mesh architectures.

Tools & Tech  
Submariner, Open Cluster Management, Fleet, K3s/K3d for edge, KubeEdge, MicroK8s, Skupper.

──────────────────────────────────────────
11. Automation, GitOps & Platform Engineering
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Provide self-service, policy-guarded platforms where everything (infra, cluster, app) is represented as code and reconciled autonomously.

Tasks  
• Architect Git repository layout (mono-repo vs. multi-repo), branching strategy, environment promotion workflows.  
• Wire pull-request checks, OPA pre-merge validation, drift detection alerts.  
• Build internal developer platforms with Backstage, Crossplane or Kratix to provision cloud resources via Kubernetes CRDs.

Concept Mastery  
• Reconciliation loops, idempotency, watch cache, finalizers, garbage collection of composite resources.  
• Secret and credential handling in GitOps pipelines (Sealed Secrets, SOPS, Mozilla sops-k8s).

Tools & Tech  
Argo CD, Flux v2, Crossplane, Terraform-controller, Backstage, Keptn, Jenkins X, Tekton, Dagger.

──────────────────────────────────────────
12. Extensibility & Custom Resources
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Extend Kubernetes API cleanly to model domain concepts, automate maintenance and integrate external systems.

Tasks  
• Design CRDs with validation schemas, conversion webhooks, subresources; implement controllers/operators with Kubebuilder, Operator-SDK, Kopf.  
• Handle leader election, rate limiting, exponential back-off and retries within controllers.  
• Publish APIs, version them (v1alpha1 -> v1beta1 -> v1), manage upgrade paths and backward compatibility.

Concept Mastery  
• API machinery (informers, listers, workqueues), custom admission webhooks, server-side apply semantics.  
• OwnerReferences, finalizers, garbage collection, aggregated API servers.

Tools & Tech  
Kubebuilder, Operator-SDK, Helm Operator, Metacontroller, Crossplane packages, CRD validation libraries, GVK conversion.

──────────────────────────────────────────
13. Ecosystem Integration & Tooling Fluency
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Seamlessly plug clusters into surrounding enterprise tooling (CI/CD, ITSM, SCM, security scanners, cloud services).

Tasks  
• Integrate container registries (Harbor, ECR, ACR, GCR), policy scanning, vulnerability remediation workflows.  
• Connect to message brokers, data pipelines, secret stores, serverless frameworks (Knative, OpenFaaS) from within Kubernetes.  
• Package and distribute workloads via OCI charts, bundles, operators.

Concept Mastery  
• OCI image spec internals, content‐addressable layers, registry authentication flows.  
• Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) channel, bundle, catalog design.

Tools & Tech  
Harbor, Notary v2, cosign, Clair, Trivy, Knative Serving/Eventing, OLM, Helm registries.

──────────────────────────────────────────
14. Process, Governance & Mentorship
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Drive adoption of Kubernetes best practices, mentor teams, codify standards, and enforce governance at scale.

Tasks  
• Create runbooks, playbooks, incident response guides, architectural decision records (ADR).  
• Lead architecture reviews, promote internal RFC process, conduct failure post-mortems using 5-whys or SRE blameless practices.  
• Provide capability uplift sessions, code reviews, shadowing, pair-debugging.

Concept Mastery  
• SRE principles (error budgets, toil, incident management), DevSecOps pipelines, compliance frameworks (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, FedRAMP) as they relate to Kubernetes.

Tools & Tech  
Incident response platforms (PagerDuty, OpsGenie), documentation tooling (mkdocs, docs-as-code), Architecture decision trackers.

──────────────────────────────────────────
15. Community Interaction & Upstream Navigation
──────────────────────────────────────────
Outcomes  
• Track roadmap, understand KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), and engage appropriately with SIGs to influence direction.

Tasks  
• Evaluate upcoming features, manage feature-gates, plan phased adoption.  
• File and triage issues, contribute bug reports or minor PRs to core or ecosystem projects, participate in SIG calls when necessary.  
• Maintain internal knowledge base on version deprecation schedules, security bulletins (CVE feeds).

Concept Mastery  
• CNCF landscape tiers, release cadence, CVSS scoring, SIG ownership model.  
• Code of Conduct, governance, licensing (Apache 2.0, SPDX).

Tools & Tech  
KEP tracker, pr-review tools, devstats, k8s-release-notes scraper, slack.k8s.io channels.

──────────────────────────────────────────
Summary
──────────────────────────────────────────
An Advanced-level Kubernetes professional must be able to own the full lifecycle of complex clusters, enact platform patterns that scale across multiple teams, deliver secure and observable production systems, and act as a multiplier for organisational capability.  They possess authoritative depth in core internals while displaying broad, working knowledge of the surrounding cloud-native ecosystem.
